<PAGE><|det|>title [114, 117, 280, 136]<|/det|>2.1.3 Audit Goals
<|det|>text [112, 171, 886, 288]<|/det|>CredShields uses both in-house tools and manual methods for comprehensive smart contract security auditing. The majority of the audit is done by manually reviewing the contract source code, following SWC registry standards, and an extended industry standard self-developed checklist. The team places emphasis on understanding core concepts, preparing test cases, and evaluating business logic for potential vulnerabilities.
<|det|>title [113, 328, 319, 349]<|/det|>2.2 Retesting Phase
<|det|>text [112, 387, 884, 429]<|/det|>Hemi Labs is actively partnering with CredShields to validate the remediations implemented towards the discovered vulnerabilities.
<|det|>title [113, 474, 549, 496]<|/det|>2.3 Vulnerability classification and severity
<|det|>text [112, 532, 884, 651]<|/det|>CredShields follows OWASP's Risk Rating Methodology to determine the risk associated with discovered vulnerabilities. This approach considers two factors – Likelihood and Impact – which are evaluated with three possible values – Low, Medium, and High, based on factors such as Threat agents, Vulnerability factors, and Technical and Business Impacts. The overall severity of the risk is calculated by combining the likelihood and impact estimates.

<|det|>text [114, 185, 378, 207]<|/det|>Bug ID #1[ Acknowledged ]
<|det|>title [113, 241, 592, 262]<|/det|>Missing zero _minOut validation while swapping
<|det|>title [113, 302, 260, 319]<|/det|>Vulnerability Type
<|det|>text [114, 321, 302, 337]<|/det|>Missing Input Validation
<|det|>title [113, 360, 185, 377]<|/det|>Severity
<|det|>text [114, 380, 154, 396]<|/det|>High
<|det|>title [113, 418, 210, 435]<|/det|>Description
<|det|>text [112, 437, 884, 531]<|/det|>The claimCompAndConvertTo() function allows swapping COMP tokens to a specified token using a DEX router. The function accepts a __minOut parameter that determines the minimum output amount when performing the swap. However, the function does not validate that this value is greater than zero. When a keeper or governor calls this function with __minOut set to 0, they effectively approve any amount of tokens in return, even if it's substantially below market value.
<|det|>title [114, 552, 231, 567]<|/det|>Affected Code
<|det|>text [142, 571, 880, 607]<|/det|>- https://github.com/hemilabs/vusd-stablecoin/blob/54f9f235f26df813152b3d3235e7f4373c e473b6/contracts/Treasury.sol#.L168-L187
<|det|>title [113, 629, 185, 644]<|/det|>Impacts
<|det|>text [112, 647, 885, 740]<|/det|>A malicious keeper can exploit this by front-running the transaction and manipulating the pool's price, causing the function to receive far fewer tokens than what would be fair for the input amount. This can lead to direct fund loss for the protocol as the swap could execute at highly unfavorable rates. MEV bots can also target these transactions, further extracting value from the protocol.
<|det|>title [113, 763, 219, 777]<|/det|>Remediation
<|det|>text [113, 782, 678, 798]<|/det|>It is recommended to add a validation to the _minOut is not equal to zero.
<|det|>title [113, 821, 174, 835]<|/det|>Retest
<|det|>text [113, 839, 655, 856]<|/det|>Client's comment: Won't fix assuming the keeper role is a trusted role.

<|det|>title [113, 170, 728, 192]<|/det|>Missing handling of fees on transfer in ERC20 token transfers
<|det|>title [113, 232, 262, 249]<|/det|>Vulnerability Type
<|det|>text [114, 251, 296, 268]<|/det|>Calculation Inaccuracy
<|det|>title [113, 290, 186, 306]<|/det|>Severity
<|det|>text [114, 309, 182, 325]<|/det|>Medium
<|det|>title [113, 348, 212, 364]<|/det|>Description
<|det|>text [112, 366, 886, 459]<|/det|>The contract contains a vulnerability related to transferring ERC20 tokens without considering the possibility of fees charged on transfer. Some ERC20 tokens implement a fee mechanism, where a certain percentage of tokens is deducted as a fee during each transfer. However, the contract does not account for this possibility when transferring tokens using the safeTransferFrom/TransferFrom function.
<|det|>title [113, 482, 234, 497]<|/det|>Affected Code
<|det|>text [142, 501, 880, 537]<|/det|>- https://github.com/hemilabs/vusd-stablecoin/blob/54f9f235f26df813152b3d3235e7f4373c e473b6/contracts/Minter.sol#L237-L249
<|det|>title [113, 559, 185, 574]<|/det|>Impacts
<|det|>text [112, 578, 886, 670]<|/det|>Failure to account for transfer fees can lead to accounting errors and financial losses. When tokens with transfer fees are transferred, the actual received amount may be less than expected due to the deduction of fees. As a result, the contract's internal accounting and balance tracking may become inaccurate, leading to discrepancies in token balances and potential financial losses for users.
<|det|>title [113, 693, 219, 707]<|/det|>Remediation
<|det|>text [112, 712, 884, 748]<|/det|>To address this vulnerability, it is recommended to add a mechanism to calculate the balance of the contract before and after the transfer is completed.

<|det|>text [113, 789, 316, 805]<|/det|>This issue has been fixed.

<PAGE><|det|>header [114, 92, 380, 113]<|/det|>Bug ID #3 [Acknowledged]
<|det|>title [112, 148, 884, 194]<|/det|>claimCompAndConvertTo() swap with 'deadline: block.timestamp' offers no protection
<|det|>title [113, 234, 260, 251]<|/det|>Vulnerability Type
<|det|>text [114, 253, 262, 269]<|/det|>Incorrect Deadline
<|det|>title [113, 292, 185, 308]<|/det|>Severity
<|det|>text [114, 311, 180, 325]<|/det|>Medium
<|det|>title [113, 350, 212, 366]<|/det|>Description
<|det|>text [112, 368, 884, 424]<|/det|>Using block.timestamp as deadline parameter in claimCompAndConvertTo() during interaction with router, which suggests that whenever the miner decides to include the transaction in a block, it will be valid at that time, since block.timestamp will be the current timestamp.
<|det|>text [112, 426, 884, 462]<|/det|>Whichever block the txn will be included in will be block.timestamp, so setting the deadline to block.timestamp offers no protection as validators can hold the transaction indefinitely.
<|det|>title [113, 483, 236, 498]<|/det|>Affected Code
<|det|>text [142, 502, 880, 539]<|/det|>- https://github.com/hemilabs/vusd-stablecoin/blob/54f9f235f26df813152b3d3235e7f4373c e473b6/contracts/Treasury.sol#L183
<|det|>title [113, 560, 182, 575]<|/det|>Impacts
<|det|>text [112, 579, 885, 690]<|/det|>It may be more profitable for a miner to deny the transaction from being mined until the transaction incurs the maximum amount of slippage. A malicious miner can hold the transaction as the deadline is set to block.timestamp, which means that whenever the miner decides to include the transaction in a block, it will be valid at that time, since block.timestamp will be the current timestamp. The transaction might be left hanging in the mempool and be executed way later than the user wanted.
<|det|>title [113, 713, 219, 727]<|/det|>Remediation
<|det|>text [112, 732, 884, 768]<|/det|>It is recommended to add a deadline argument to the claimCompAndConvertTo() function that interacts with the router, and pass it along to the router calls.
<|det|>title [113, 790, 172, 805]<|/det|>Retest
<|det|>text [112, 809, 763, 825]<|/det|>Client's comment: will fix it in future when we have plan to update treasury contract.
